title: Accelerating Rare Disease Diagnostic Pathways
business: Specialized clinical genetics laboratories tasked with diagnosing rare pediatric conditions.
problem: Geneticists face significant delays in diagnostic workflows because manually cross-referencing patient variants against rapidly evolving biomedical literature is time-intensive and prone to missing obscure, recently published case studies.
solution: The PubMed connector integrates directly into the Claude interface, allowing the laboratory team to automate the retrieval of peer-reviewed literature. By using the connector, the team can query specific genetic variants or clinical phenotypes directly against the PubMed database, surfacing relevant abstracts and full-text articles from PubMed Central without leaving the analysis environment.
steps: Configure the PubMed connector within the Claude workspace to enable secure access to the PubMed API endpoints.
Define a structured prompt that extracts patient phenotype data and converts it into search queries for the search_articles tool.
Execute iterative searches to retrieve metadata and abstracts for high-confidence matches related to the patient's genetic profile.
Utilize the get_full_text_article tool to extract detailed clinical findings from PMC-indexed papers for final review by the lead geneticist.
outcome: The laboratory achieves a more efficient literature review process, enabling faster synthesis of evidence for rare disease diagnoses and reducing the cognitive load on clinical staff.
limitation: The connector is limited to content indexed in PubMed and PubMed Central; it cannot access proprietary journals or non-indexed institutional repositories. Users must verify the source coverage by checking the PubMed indexing status of their required journals.

The inability of geneticists to communicate with patients regarding their diagnosis.
The high cost of purchasing subscriptions to proprietary medical journals.
